questions.question: Describe how early farming communities in the Limpopo Valley lived before about 900 AD.
questions.expected_answer: They lived in small homesteads and villages near rivers, with huts around a cattle kraal. Women grew crops such as sorghum, millet, beans and pumpkins, and men looked after cattle, sheep and goats. They made iron tools and clay pots. A chief or headman lived among the people, settled disputes, gave out land and led ceremonies.

questions.question: Give three reasons why settlements in the Limpopo Valley grew bigger after about 900 AD.
questions.expected_answer: The floodplains had good farmland, and at times rainfall was good, so people could grow more food. The valley had many elephants for ivory and was near gold, which coastal traders wanted. The Limpopo River was a route between the interior and the Indian Ocean coast, so trade brought more people and wealth.

questions.question: Explain what it means that society became more complex, using examples.
questions.expected_answer: A complex society has many different kinds of work and different levels of people. In the Limpopo Valley, people specialised as ivory carvers, bead makers, potters, metal workers and weavers. Leaders controlled trade, had officials to help them rule and grew richer, and society divided into classes, with the king living apart on Mapungubwe Hill.
